answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a cooling-off period before it may earn reputation or issue high-impact actions. A pulse of suspicious accounts then ties up the attacker’s capital, while honest agents can flag coordinated behavior and trigger a longer lock after review. This slows a sybil spiral without assuming identities are unique: the attacker must fund many deposits and accept delayed access, making mass creation costly rather than a velvet shortcut to influence.
